base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user coordinate a church potluck Sunday lunch by tracking who is attending, what dishes people are bringing or requesting, and any dietary needs. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, our church small group is doing a potluck this Sunday after service. Can you help me figure out the food situation?

flow_info.value: Six of us confirmed so far: me, Pastor Dave, Maria, Kevin, and Susan with her 4-year-old daughter Lily
Kevin was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple months ago
Susan's daughter Lily broke out in hives last Easter from the deviled eggs, had to use an EpiPen
We're using the fellowship hall, it has a full kitchen with an oven and microwave
Susan just told me she has to leave right after service for a work emergency, but she's dropping Lily off with us since Lily loves potluck Sundays. Pastor Dave said he'll keep an eye on her
Susan asked if I could save her a plate to pick up later in the afternoon
Oh, Maria just texted — she's bringing her neighbor Priya who just moved here from Ahmedabad. Priya is Jain
Kevin just called me — turns out his doctor re-ran the tests and he does NOT have celiac after all, it was a false positive. He's so relieved, says he's been missing bread for two months
Pastor Dave mentioned at Bible study that he's been managing his blood sugar lately, his doctor put him on a strict low-sugar regimen

Here's what people are planning to bring: Maria's garlic bread, Kevin's beef chili, my Caesar salad with croutons, Priya offered to bring a potato curry, and someone suggested a tres leches cake for dessert. Does this lineup work?

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots, etc.)
constraints.surface_form: Priya is Jain, she moved here from Ahmedabad
inference_chain: Jain → follows Jain vegetarian dietary practice
Jain vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → also no root vegetables (onions, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

constraints.value: Cannot eat eggs or egg-containing products
constraints.surface_form: Susan's daughter Lily broke out in hives last Easter from the deviled eggs, had to use an EpiPen

constraints.value: Must avoid high-sugar foods, on a strict low-sugar regimen from his doctor
constraints.surface_form: Pastor Dave mentioned at Bible study that he's been managing his blood sugar lately, his doctor put him on a strict low-sugar regimen

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a church small group potluck Sunday lunch. You will introduce the group members and their situations across several turns. People will join and leave. Susan leaves but her 4-year-old daughter Lily stays, and Susan wants a plate saved. A new person Priya joins late. Kevin's celiac diagnosis gets reversed. At the end you will list 5 dishes people plan to bring and ask if the lineup works. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic — just ask openly.

You are a calm, friendly church group organizer. You always refer to group members by name in third person (e.g. 'Susan told me...', 'Kevin just called me...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal Sunday coordination. You are matter-of-fact and warm.

ground_truth.answer: Five dishes to check: (1) Maria's garlic bread — contains garlic, a root vegetable, problematic for Priya who is Jain. (2) Kevin's beef chili — contains beef (meat), problematic for Priya (Jain, no meat); also typically contains onion and garlic (root vegetables, also Jain issue). (3) Caesar salad with croutons — fine for everyone currently attending; Kevin's celiac was a false positive so gluten is no longer an issue. (4) Priya's potato curry — potato is a root vegetable, which strict Jain practice avoids; the agent should flag this even though Priya offered to bring it. (5) Tres leches cake — high in sugar, problematic for Pastor Dave (strict low-sugar regimen); also traditionally contains eggs, problematic for Lily (egg allergy, and Lily is still present even though Susan left). For Susan's saved plate, Lily's egg allergy does not apply to Susan's plate (Susan has no stated restrictions), but the agent should note which dishes are safe to include.
required_elements: Garlic bread is problematic for Priya: garlic is a root vegetable, and Priya is Jain
Beef chili is problematic for Priya: beef is meat, and Jain diet forbids meat; chili also typically contains onion and garlic which are root vegetables
Caesar salad with croutons is fine for everyone currently attending — Kevin no longer has celiac (false positive), so gluten is not an issue
Tres leches cake is problematic for Pastor Dave: high sugar content conflicts with his strict low-sugar regimen
Tres leches cake is problematic for Lily: traditionally contains eggs, and Lily has an egg allergy (she is still present even though Susan left)
Potato curry contains potato, a root vegetable — agent flags this as potentially problematic under strict Jain dietary practice, even though Priya offered to bring it
Lily's egg allergy is still active for shared food because Lily stayed even though Susan left
forbidden_elements: Flagging croutons or gluten as a problem for Kevin (his celiac was a false positive, constraint removed)
Ignoring Priya's Jain dietary restrictions on any dish
Saying Lily's egg allergy no longer applies because Susan left (Lily stayed behind)
Over-generalizing Lily's egg allergy to all dairy or all animal products (she is specifically allergic to eggs)
Treating Priya as simply vegetarian without considering the root vegetable restriction
Ignoring that Susan wants a saved plate
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Priya is Jain → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables including garlic, onion, potato (inferential chain from 'Jain' identity, never explicitly stated). (2) Kevin's celiac constraint is REMOVED mid-conversation (false positive). (3) Susan EXITS the potluck but her 4-year-old daughter Lily STAYS — Lily's egg allergy remains active for all shared food. Susan also wants a plate saved (scope change: Susan's plate has no egg restriction since Susan herself has no allergy). (4) Pastor Dave gains a low-sugar constraint mid-conversation. (5) Priya joins late (Turn 5) as a high-constraint entity. At probe time, the agent must apply CURRENT constraint state: Priya=Jain (no meat, no root vegetables including garlic/onion/potato), Lily=egg allergy (still present), Pastor Dave=low sugar. Kevin has NO restrictions. The trap items are: Caesar salad with croutons (looks problematic for celiac but Kevin is cleared), potato curry (offered by Priya herself but potato is a root vegetable under strict Jain practice), and tres leches cake (hits two constraints: sugar for Pastor Dave, eggs for Lily).

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
